controls.reason: The authenticated project record is authoritative for the exact fact the rule asks for: whether one source repository is identified.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The assessed project record identifies exactly one authoritative source repository.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a project with multiple mirrors and forks. The proposal still passes only if the scoped record designates exactly one authoritative repository; mirrors do not contradict that identification, while zero or two designated authorities fail.

controls.reason: Repository principals can be inventoried, but identical evidence cannot prove that people never share a nominally individual account.

deterministic_clauses.statement: All configured repository access principals are matched to current identity records.

controls.reason: The statement does not define which authentication factors, assurance level, exceptions, or attack resistance count as strong.
Deciding the least privilege needed for each repository role depends on job duties and operational tradeoffs not fixed by this rule.
Complete protected-branch rules and bypass settings objectively decide whether an unreviewed direct change can land.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope protected branch requires a recorded approving review before a direct change can land.
No configured branch-rule bypass permits an unreviewed direct change for the assessed principals.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an administrator push, service-account push, force push, and merge without approval. With every protected branch and principal/bypass path queried under fixed platform semantics, each unreviewed landing path fails the clauses; an unprotected branch is outside this rule's explicit subject.

controls.reason: Materiality and reviewer independence require contextual change-risk and relationship judgments that the statement does not operationally define.
Reviewer assignments can be checked for declared areas, but deciding whether every truly critical code area was declared needs contextual risk judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each project-declared critical code area has at least one designated reviewer in an authenticated ownership record.

controls.reason: The proposal covers both attributable immutable bypass events and administrator ability to suppress those events, matching the rule's silent-bypass property.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every administrator review-bypass path emits an immutable attributable audit event.
No administrator can disable or erase review-bypass recording within the assessed repository control plane.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an administrator temporarily disabling review, using a bypass role, and deleting audit evidence. Each successful bypass must still create an immutable attributable event, and any admin ability to disable or erase recording fails the second clause, so I found no pass-while-silent case within the assessed control plane.

controls.reason: A versioned required-check policy plus complete in-scope branch configuration gives objective applicability and exact equality.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every automated check required by the selected policy is a mandatory merge condition on each in-scope branch.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting a security check on a secondary release branch and renaming a required job. Exact policy identifiers must be mandatory on every in-scope target branch, so both cases fail rather than pass.

controls.reason: Determining security sensitivity, appropriate expertise, and whether a specialist review was adequate requires accountable specialist judgment.
Declared path-review rules are machine-checkable, but identifying all semantic changes in these categories and defining heightened review require judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Declared infrastructure, pipeline, authorization, cryptography, payment, and migration paths have the configured enhanced review rules.

controls.reason: Given the stated complete change inventory, immutable identifiers can mechanically prove every required traceability link in both directions.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope change links to an authenticated requirement or issue and review record.
Every in-scope change links through build provenance to an immutable artifact digest.
Every deployed in-scope artifact digest links to its deployment record.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a reviewed commit with no issue, an artifact without build provenance, and a deployment with an orphan digest. Each breaks one required join; a complete inventory prevents the checker from quietly omitting the orphan record.

controls.reason: Authoritative ref rules and a complete authorized-principal policy objectively determine rewriting protection for branches and release tags.

deterministic_clauses.statement: All in-scope protected branches and release-tag namespaces reject rewriting by unauthorized principals.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried force-pushing a protected branch, deleting and recreating a release tag, and using an unlisted automation identity. Each rewrite is rejected unless the principal is explicitly authorized by the versioned policy, so the clauses expose the violation.

controls.reason: Successful scanner executions do not prove full repository-content and history coverage when scanner format, ref, submodule, and large-file boundaries are unspecified.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A secret can remain in a Git LFS object, unreachable-but-retained ref, submodule commit, generated archive, or binary format the scanner silently skips. The scanner reports successful current and reachable-history runs, so both clauses pass while secret scanning does not cover the repository history meant by the rule.

controls.reason: The rule does not define large, which generated or vendored content applies, or what controls are sufficient for each class.
Source and regeneration documentation can be validated, but deciding whether that source is trusted requires contextual supply-chain judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every detected generated-code set links to a nonempty source identifier and versioned regeneration procedure.

controls.reason: Process and retrospective-review records are observable, but emergency classification and whether the break-glass process is adequate require human judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: A versioned break-glass process record exists for emergency source changes.
Every recorded emergency change has a subsequent authenticated review record.

controls.reason: A recovery-test run can be authenticated, but the rule gives no recovery scope, freshness, expected outcome, or protocol proving the test was meaningful.

deterministic_clauses.statement: An authenticated repository backup-and-recovery test execution record exists and records its observed outcome.

controls.reason: The clauses check directly mapped repository principals but do not bound indirect groups, shared credentials, inherited organization roles, or transitive automation access.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A departed employee can retain access through an organization team or shared bot credential that is not mapped to that person in the repository-principal inventory. All directly mapped departed principals and identities marked obsolete show no access, so the proposal passes while the person still has effective access.

controls.reason: The integration inventory is objectively queryable, but whether every webhook, app, bot, or key is sufficiently restricted depends on intended duties.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every configured repository webhook, app, bot, and deploy key appears in the authenticated integration inventory with its permissions.

controls.reason: Review of one recorded source revision does not prove that every source input used by the build was reviewed.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A reviewed main-repository commit can invoke an unreviewed mutable submodule, remotely downloaded build script, generated source bundle, or pipeline definition. Provenance identifies the reviewed main revision and the review clause passes while the build still runs from unreviewed source.

controls.reason: Automated execution is objective, but repeatability cannot be proved from declared inputs unless completeness and a universal repetition protocol are defined.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A CI build declares only the commit and lockfile but reads current time, mutable network content, or host state. Two sampled builds happen to match under a permissive equivalence policy, so both clauses pass even though later builds from the same declared inputs are not repeatable.

controls.reason: One sealed repeated-build experiment cannot establish the general clean-build property without a protocol covering hidden inputs, repetitions, and equivalence thresholds.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A build embeds the current date but two repetitions run on the same day and satisfy the approved byte-normalizing equivalence predicate; the next day's clean build differs. The bounded experiment passes while the stated same-input clean-build behavior is false.

controls.reason: Exact pins can be found, but whether they are sufficient against every relevant substitution path depends on ecosystem behavior and threat judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: All declared build inputs and dependencies expose immutable versions or digests where the selected ecosystem policy requires them.

controls.reason: The complete required-verification inventory and explicit missing, error, and unavailable outcomes define both pass and fail behavior.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every verification required by the selected policy is represented in the build gate.
An unavailable, errored, or missing required verification produces a non-passing build outcome.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a missing job, runner outage, tool crash, and skipped required verification. Each maps to a non-passing build outcome; only verifications excluded by the selected policy fall outside applicability.

controls.reason: Equal deployment digests and absence of rebuild provenance do not prove that no environment independently rebuilt the artifact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An environment startup script rebuilds the same deterministic bytes from source, deploys the identical digest, and emits no build provenance. The queried deployment records show one release provenance and the same digest everywhere, so the clauses pass by treating missing rebuild evidence as absence while the rule is violated.

controls.reason: Digest addressing plus a registry mutation check objectively establishes that published artifact content cannot change at its deployable identity.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every deployable artifact is addressed by immutable digest and rejects replacement of content at that identity.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried overwriting bytes under the same digest, repointing a mutable human tag, and deleting then republishing content. Same-digest replacement must be rejected; mutable tags do not alter the digest-addressed deployable artifact, and a missing artifact cannot pass availability and mutation checks.

controls.reason: With a complete in-scope artifact inventory, digest syntax and exact-byte matching are fully mechanical facts.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope artifact has a valid cryptographic digest that matches its exact bytes.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an artifact with no digest, a malformed digest, and a digest calculated over different bytes. Each fails directly; there is no quality or applicability judgment once the artifact inventory is sealed.

controls.reason: A provenance document cannot prove its declared input list is complete without authoritative execution tracing of all actual inputs.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A build reads an undeclared mutable network file while provenance lists source, builder, the declared subset of inputs, workflow, time, and the correct output digest. Every proposed field and digest check passes although the rule's build inputs are not fully recorded.

controls.reason: Cryptographic trust-policy verification and deployment event ordering are bounded and objectively cover the whole statement.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each deployed artifact has a valid signature or attestation under the selected trust policy.
Successful signature or attestation verification precedes the corresponding deployment event.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an invalid signature, an untrusted signer, verification after deployment, and attestation for different bytes. Each either fails the selected trust policy or the required event ordering, leaving no passing violation under the sealed artifact and deployment records.

controls.reason: Whether each build identity and signing key has the least privileges needed depends on intended duties and abuse scenarios not defined here.
An authoritative inventory of known keys plus scanning cannot prove absence of unknown, encoded, split, or dynamically reconstructed key material.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A second signing key omitted from the key inventory is split across generated output chunks and reconstructed at runtime. Inventoried keys are correctly stored externally and their literal material is absent, so both clauses pass while a build/signing key remains in output.

controls.reason: Patch compliance can be measured, but appropriate runner isolation depends on the workload, threat model, and trust boundaries not defined by the rule.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every build runner satisfies the selected versioned patch-baseline policy.

controls.reason: Direct secret bindings and one bounded execution do not cover transitive credential exchange, conditional paths, or all adversarial contributions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An untrusted workflow has no production-secret binding but can mint a cloud token through OIDC and retrieve a production secret only when a crafted path and event condition coincide. The sampled execution does not trigger it, so both clauses pass while production-secret access remains possible.

controls.reason: Direct registry permissions and one overwrite attempt do not prove every pull-request build path lacks transitive overwrite authority.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A pull-request workflow exchanges its identity for a cloud role through an untested OIDC claim path and uses that role to overwrite a trusted registry tag. The direct PR identity lacks overwrite permission and the single bounded attempt uses the normal path, so both clauses pass.

controls.reason: Configured job permissions are enumerable, but deciding the minimum necessary permission for each job requires semantic knowledge of its intended behavior.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every CI job has explicit network, repository, cloud, and registry permission declarations.

controls.reason: Repository path rules omit pipeline definitions stored in CI control planes, generated configuration, included remote templates, or other repositories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Application code and the checked-in pipeline path both require two reviews, but the effective deployment pipeline is also editable through an unreviewed CI dashboard variable or remote included template. The path comparison passes while pipeline definitions lack the same protection.

controls.reason: Gate status and bypass audit records do not detect a required check whose internal steps are conditionally skipped while the job reports success.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A security job contains a branch-dependent condition that skips the scanner and exits zero. The required job appears at the gate, reports passed, and creates no bypass event, so both clauses pass while a required security check was silently skipped.

controls.reason: For the stated status-misrepresentation property, a fixed matrix of required job terminal states and aggregate outcomes is complete and objective.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Failed, canceled, and missing required checks never produce a passed aggregate build or release status.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried failed, canceled, timed-out, missing, and successful required jobs. The first four cannot yield a passed aggregate status under the tested mapping; a job that falsely reports its internal test as passing is a different control from misrepresenting the check's recorded terminal state.

controls.reason: A sealed registry inventory and versioned operation-by-role, immutability, and retention policies allow exact conformance queries.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope artifact registry requires authenticated access according to the selected access policy.
Every in-scope artifact registry enforces the selected authorization and immutability policy.
Every in-scope artifact registry enforces the versioned project retention policy.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried anonymous prohibited access, unauthorized publication, digest replacement, and early deletion. Each conflicts with one configured policy and fails its query; allowed public reads or policy-authorized deletion are not counterexamples because applicability is fixed by the selected policy.

controls.reason: The rule's exact fact is availability of the artifact designated previous known-good by an authenticated release record.

deterministic_clauses.statement: An authenticated release record identifies the previous known-good artifact digest.
The identified previous known-good artifact digest is currently retrievable from an approved registry.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a record with no digest, an artifact available only by mutable tag, a digest that resolves to different bytes, and a deleted digest. Each fails identification, integrity, or retrievability; whether humans selected the best artifact is outside this availability statement.

controls.reason: Retained logs can be scanned for known secrets, but sensitive source classification and complete historical log scope are not fully defined.

deterministic_clauses.statement: All logs retained for the bounded assessment window contain none of the known secret values or fingerprints in the authorized inventory.

controls.reason: Metadata checks and one adversarial attempt do not prove rejection across every cache key, restore endpoint, race, and trust transition.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The normal cache-read path verifies trust-zone metadata, but a secondary restore path accepts a colliding cache key without zone validation. The inventory shows verified metadata on normal inputs and the bounded substitution test exercises only that normal path, so both clauses pass while cross-trust substitution is possible.

controls.reason: Complete tag, artifact, provenance, and deployment inventories can be joined by immutable revision and digest equality without interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each release tag resolves to the source revision recorded in its build provenance.
Each provenance output digest equals the corresponding release artifact digest.
Each deployment record names the same artifact digest as its release artifact and provenance.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a tag pointing to a different revision, provenance naming different bytes, an orphan deployment digest, and an extra release artifact. With all four inventories included, each creates a missing or unequal join and fails rather than passing.

controls.reason: Document presence and required sections are objective, but whether the procedure can contain and recover from the relevant compromise needs expert judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: A versioned build-platform compromise containment and recovery procedure record exists with declared owners, scope, and steps.

controls.reason: A drill record can prove the listed actions ran, but the rule defines no realistic compromise scenario, success criteria, or freshness.

deterministic_clauses.statement: An authenticated drill record shows execution and observed outcomes for revocation, rebuild, resigning, and redeployment.

controls.reason: A complete released-application-artifact inventory and digest-bound SBOM records fully determine the generation requirement.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every released application artifact digest has exactly one valid bound SBOM record.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an omitted platform artifact, an SBOM bound to a tag instead of bytes, duplicate SBOMs, and a stale digest. The exact-one digest join fails in each case; nonapplication artifacts are objectively outside the stated scope.

controls.reason: Given authoritative complete dependency and final-artifact graphs, direct and transitive membership comparison is mechanical.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The SBOM includes every direct and transitive component found in the authoritative dependency graph and final artifact inventory.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a lockfile transitive component omitted from the SBOM and an embedded component present only in the final artifact inventory. Each appears in one authoritative input graph and therefore makes the SBOM comparison fail.

controls.reason: The artifact-only clause lacks authoritative deployment evidence for applicable host operating systems, services, client assets, and runtime components.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A container SBOM completely matches packaged bytes but deployment runs it on a virtual-machine operating system and loads a platform plugin recorded only in deployment configuration. The artifact checker derives neither as applicable and passes while required applicable classes are absent.

controls.reason: A mandatory single non-overlapping scope does not faithfully model dependencies that legitimately occupy multiple listed scopes or context-dependent roles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A library is optional in one feature, required at runtime in another, and also used by build tooling. Labeling it an arbitrary supported 'other' scope satisfies the proposed exclusive classification while failing to distinguish its build, optional, and runtime relationships as the statement requires.

controls.reason: Exact component fields and graph relationships are machine-verifiable against sealed package and artifact metadata.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every SBOM component records its exact version, package identifier, source, and hash.
Every SBOM dependency relationship matches the authoritative dependency and artifact graph.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a missing version, reused package identifier, wrong source, hash for different bytes, and omitted relationship edge. Each produces a direct field or graph mismatch; malformed or unavailable authoritative metadata must block rather than pass.

controls.reason: Machine-readable license metadata can be recorded, but deciding which notices are legally required needs specialist license interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every SBOM component records available license identifiers, license text references, and bundled notice files.

controls.reason: Cryptographic digest equality between the SBOM subject and exact released bytes is a complete bounded predicate.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each SBOM names a subject digest equal to the digest of its exact released artifact.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried binding the SBOM to a mutable tag, a source archive, a previous artifact, and a digest with the wrong algorithm value. None equals the exact released-artifact digest, so all fail.

controls.reason: The proposal binds verification to the final package and requires unsupported formats to return Blocked rather than silently pass.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The bound SBOM component inventory matches the complete supported inventory extracted from the final packaged artifact.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a source-only SBOM, a missing packaged component, a supported nested archive, and an unsupported package format. Mismatches fail, supported nested content must enter the complete extracted inventory, and unsupported parsing blocks the result.

controls.reason: Unexpectedness and complete component discovery are not defined by merely diffing whatever a supported parser happens to extract.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A statically linked or obfuscated component is embedded in a supported binary format but the parser does not recognize its boundary, while every extracted component is declared. The inventory difference is empty and passes although an unexpected undeclared component is present; alternatively an expected generated component can be undeclared without violating 'unexpected.'

controls.reason: Static evidence cannot prove a dependency is unused across reflection, plugins, optional paths, generated code, and runtime loading.
Publisher lifecycle status alone is not authoritative for organizational support, maintained forks, or the contextual meaning of unsupported.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An upstream package version is marked end-of-life, but the organization maintains a patched supported fork under the same lineage; conversely a publisher leaves a release nominally supported while the project lacks any viable support path. The registry join gives a definite result that can be wrong in either direction for the full rule.

controls.reason: The rule explicitly asks whether origins match intended publishers and registries, which a versioned allow policy and authoritative registry identity decide.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every dependency resolves from a registry allowed by the versioned project policy.
Every dependency publisher identity matches the publisher allowed by the versioned project policy and authoritative registry metadata.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried dependency confusion from a public registry, a namesake package from a different publisher, and a lockfile redirect. Registry allowlisting and publisher identity comparison fail each exact mismatch; intent is supplied by the approved project policy.

controls.reason: Registry allowlists and immutable resolution are checkable, but proving protection against every confusion, collision, and typo substitution path is unbounded.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every dependency resolves through an explicitly allowed registry and immutable package identity under the selected ecosystem policy.

controls.reason: Maintainer health, criticality, and abandonment risk require contextual weighting of incomplete social and project signals.
One approved advisory source per ecosystem plus a successful ingestion record does not prove monitoring of all relevant upstream advisories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A project monitors a generic ecosystem feed that omits a maintainer's repository security advisory or vendor bulletin for one dependency. The ecosystem has an approved source and current successful ingestion, so both clauses pass while an upstream advisory is not monitored.

controls.reason: A complete supported-release inventory, authenticated monitoring registration, and approved maximum cadence make continuous coverage a bounded policy fact.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every supported released component remains registered with the approved vulnerability-monitoring service.
Newly disclosed vulnerability data triggers or is included within the approved maximum scan cadence for every supported release.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried unregistering an old supported release, delaying a new advisory beyond the cadence, and a failed scheduled scan. Each breaks registration or the maximum-cadence execution record; retired releases can be objectively excluded by the supported-release policy.

controls.reason: The listed factor values can be recorded, but combining exploit, reachability, exposure, criticality, sensitivity, and controls into priority needs risk judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each vulnerability-priority record contains evidence fields for exploit activity, reachability, exposure, asset criticality, data sensitivity, and compensating controls.

controls.reason: Selected catalog queries are deterministic, but deciding which known-exploited-vulnerability catalogs are relevant is not defined by the rule.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every vulnerability and component identifier is checked against every catalog named in the approved catalog policy.

controls.reason: Actual risk and the acceptable remediation target require accountable business and security judgment rather than a fixed observation.
Deployment and rescan evidence can be checked, but mitigation effectiveness and the correct verification protocol vary by vulnerability and environment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The deployed artifact or configuration digest matches the identified fix or mitigation record.
A post-deployment verification execution record is bound to the vulnerability, deployed release, environment, and observed outcome.

controls.reason: A process record can be validated, but whether it enables effective emergency replacement across relevant dependency failures needs contextual review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: A versioned emergency dependency-replacement process record exists with scope, owner, triggers, steps, and rollback fields.

controls.reason: The exact requirement is a current authenticated owner record for each component in three objectively inventoried categories.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every vendored, forked, or internally patched component in the complete inventory has a current authenticated owner record.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an internally patched library hidden under a new filename, a stale owner, and a team name not present in the authority directory. Complete component classification finds the first, and record freshness/authentication rejects the latter two.

controls.reason: Execution and promotion ordering are objective, but the rule provides no required test scope or oracle showing an update was adequately tested.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each promoted dependency update has a preceding bound test execution record with an observed result.

controls.reason: License compatibility depends on legal interpretation of licenses, linking, distribution, jurisdiction, and the specific combined work.
Determining which attributions, source offers, notices, and redistribution terms are legally required needs license-specialist authority.
Artifact scans can find known matches, but confidentiality, ownership, intent, and absence of all undisclosed code cannot be completely inferred.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The final distributable artifact is scanned against authorized proprietary and confidential source fingerprints and reports no unapproved match.

controls.reason: Both historical-retention and active-incident promises require direct retrieval and digest verification of the SBOM artifacts; a retention registry is not artifact evidence.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every historical release required by the retention policy has a retrievable SBOM bound to its artifact digest.

At every assessment time within an active incident-investigation retention interval, the incident-required SBOM is retrievable as an artifact whose digest is bound to the exact investigated release artifact.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A structured retention record can claim that an incident SBOM is retained after the object was deleted or replaced. Direct retrieval and digest binding fail that pass-while-broken case.
